record.paper_title: Some open problems in random matrix theory and the theory of integrable systems
record.original_question: For random matrix ensembles with symmetry classes β=1 and β=4, prove bulk and edge universality for general potentials of the form Q(x)=N V(x), especially when the associated equilibrium measure is supported on several disjoint intervals, rather than only for the already understood polynomial-potential cases with one-cut support. More broadly, determine whether the newer methods developed for unitary ensembles can be adapted to these orthogonal and symplectic ensembles, and resolve the long-standing conjecture that Wigner matrices also exhibit bulk universality.

evidence.quote: It is of considerable interest to prove universality in the cases β = 1 and β = 4 for more general potentials Q(x), in particular for Q(x) of the form (4) Q(x) = NV (x), where V (x), is, say, a polynomial.
It is a long-standing conjecture, now more than forty years old, that universality is also true in the bulk, but there has been very little progress.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider random matrix ensembles on the space of N×N real symmetric matrices (symmetry class β=1) and on the space of N×N quaternion self-dual matrices (symmetry class β=4) with joint eigenvalue density proportional to

  ∏_{1≤i<j≤N} |x_i − x_j|^β · exp(−∑_{i=1}^N Q(x_i)),

where the external potential has the scaling form Q(x) = N·V(x) for a sufficiently regular function V: ℝ → ℝ (e.g. polynomial or real-analytic) such that the corresponding equilibrium measure μ_V (the unique minimizer of the logarithmic energy functional with external field V) has compact support that may consist of several disjoint intervals (the "multi-cut" regime).

(a) Bulk universality. Prove that for any point x_0 in the interior of the support of μ_V where the equilibrium density ρ_V(x_0) > 0, the rescaled k-point correlation functions

  (1/(Nρ_V(x_0)))^k · R_k^{(N)}(x_0 + y_1/(Nρ_V(x_0)), …, x_0 + y_k/(Nρ_V(x_0)))

converge as N → ∞ to the universal sine-kernel correlation functions of the Gaussian Orthogonal Ensemble (β=1) and Gaussian Symplectic Ensemble (β=4) respectively.

(b) Edge universality. Prove that at a soft edge of supp(μ_V), the rescaled correlation functions converge to the universal Airy-type correlation functions associated to the GOE (β=1) and GSE (β=4).

(c) Determine whether the analytic / Riemann–Hilbert / resolvent / Dyson Brownian motion methods that have been developed for the unitary (β=2) ensembles can be adapted to obtain (a) and (b) for the orthogonal and symplectic ensembles in the multi-cut, non-polynomial case.

(d) Wigner bulk universality. Let W_N be an N×N real symmetric (resp. complex Hermitian, resp. quaternion self-dual) random matrix whose entries on and above the diagonal are independent, centered, with variance 1/N (suitably normalized), and otherwise of arbitrary common distribution (a "Wigner matrix"). Prove that, after rescaling by the local density of the semicircle law at any energy x_0 in the bulk (−2, 2), the local k-point eigenvalue correlation functions converge as N → ∞ to those of the GOE (resp. GUE, resp. GSE).
artifact.status_search_result: Both parts have been largely resolved since the problem was posed. The Wigner–Dyson–Mehta bulk universality conjecture for Wigner matrices was proved around 2009–2012 by Erdős–Schlein–Yau (with Péché, Ramírez, Yin) and independently by Tao–Vu, for all symmetry classes under mild moment conditions. For invariant β=1 and β=4 ensembles with general potentials, bulk and edge universality have been established by Shcherbina (multi-cut polynomial and analytic potentials), Krishnapur–Rider–Virág, Bourgade–Erdős–Yau (general β-ensembles, including bulk and edge universality for analytic and C^4 potentials), and via transport methods by Bekerman–Figalli–Guionnet, covering the multi-cut regime as well. Thus the open problem is essentially solved.

status_evidence.title: Bulk universality for generalized Wigner matrices
status_evidence.snippet: Erdős–Yau–Yin proof of bulk universality for generalized Wigner matrices.

status_evidence.title: Bulk Universality for Wigner Matrices (Tao–Vu)
status_evidence.snippet: Tao and Vu prove bulk universality for Wigner Hermitian matrices via the four moment theorem.
status_evidence.claim: Independent solution of Wigner bulk universality.

status_evidence.title: The Wigner-Dyson-Mehta bulk universality conjecture for Wigner matrices
status_evidence.snippet: Joint Erdős–Ramírez–Schlein–Tao–Vu–Yau paper establishes the conjecture for all Wigner matrices with exponential decay; later improved to finite moments.
status_evidence.claim: Conjecture established for broad class of Wigner matrices.

status_evidence.title: Universality of General β-Ensembles (Bourgade–Erdős–Yau)
status_evidence.snippet: Proves bulk universality of β-ensembles for any β>0 with general analytic / C^4 potentials, including multi-cut.
status_evidence.claim: Bulk universality for β=1,4 invariant ensembles with general potentials proved.

status_evidence.title: Edge Universality for Orthogonal Ensembles of Random Matrices (Shcherbina)
status_evidence.snippet: Shcherbina proves edge universality for orthogonal ensembles with polynomial potentials, including multi-cut.
status_evidence.claim: Edge universality for β=1 with general polynomial potentials proved.

status_evidence.title: Transport Maps for β-Matrix Models and Universality (Bekerman–Figalli–Guionnet)
status_evidence.snippet: Transport methods yield bulk and edge universality for β-ensembles with general potentials.
status_evidence.claim: Provides additional resolution including multi-cut regime.
